title: Request for email communications of certain village board members

communications.subject: Wisconsin Open Records Act Request: Request for email communications of certain village board members
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Wisconsin Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Electronic copies of the following public records for the period of May 1, 2026, through September 24, 2026:

1. Email Communications

Copies of all emails sent or received by Village Board members Donald Kern, Jessica Plourde, or Chris Dubek during the period identified above that relate to, concern, discuss, reference, or arise from the business, affairs, governance, operations, activities, policies, finances, personnel, services, property, proceedings, or functions of the Village of Somerset.

This request includes responsive emails:

sent or received through a Village of Somerset email account;
sent or received through a personal, private, business, or other non-Village email account when the communication relates to Village of Somerset business;
exchanged between or among any of the four Board members identified above;
exchanged between any identified Board member and any other Village Board member;
exchanged between an identified Board member and Village employees, officers, officials, committee or commission members, consultants, contractors, vendors, attorneys, or members of the public; and
on which an identified Board member was the sender, recipient, copied recipient (cc), or blind-copied recipient (bcc), to the extent a responsive record exists.

For purposes of this request, “Village of Somerset business” should be construed broadly to include any matter involving the Village of Somerset or the performance, discussion, consideration, or exercise of the duties or responsibilities of a Village Board member. 

2. Scope of Search

This request is intended to encompass responsive public records based upon their content and relationship to Village business, rather than solely upon the ownership of the device, account, or system on which the record is located.

Accordingly, please include responsive records concerning Village business maintained through personal accounts or devices to the extent such records constitute public records subject to Wisconsin's Public Records Law.

3. Withheld Records

If any responsive record is withheld in whole or in part, or any information is redacted, please identify the record or category of records withheld or redacted and provide the statutory or other legal authority supporting the withholding or redaction.

If the Village determines that any portion of this request is insufficiently specific under Wis. Stat. § 19.35(1)(h), please identify the particular portion considered insufficiently specific and the basis for that determination so that the scope may be clarified without delaying production of records responsive to the remainder of the request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

John Brannon

communications.subject: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request: Consumer complaints about the Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit calculation in Intuit TurboTax and ProSeries: how many, what the Attorney General told Intuit and consumers, referrals to Treasury, and whether an
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

In one sentence: this request asks how the Department of Attorney General handled consumer complaints about a Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit calculation error in Intuit Inc.'s tax software, what it asked Intuit, what it told consumers, and whether it opened an inquiry.

Context, from public sources. Intuit Inc. states on its TurboTax support site, in the article "Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit, Tax Year 2022", that "Some Michigan TurboTax customers have overpaid their state taxes due to an error with the Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit," and stated on its ProSeries community board on April 23, 2024 that the Michigan EITC calculation was incorrect for part-year resident filers in its tax year 2022 and 2023 Michigan programs, with corrections released March 7, 2024 and April 18, 2024. Records released by the Department of Treasury under FOIA on July 28 and August 11, 2026 show that Intuit informed Treasury of the issue on March 13, 2024 and that Treasury answered on March 20, 2024 that affected taxpayers would need to file amended returns. A consumer complaint concerning the issue was referred by the Department of Attorney General to Treasury's Bureau of Tax Policy on or about May 7, 2026.

Definitions. "The Issue" means the eligibility for, or computation of, the Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit for part-year resident or nonresident filers in tax preparation software distributed by Intuit Inc. (TurboTax, ProSeries, ProConnect or Lacerte), including the corrections Intuit released on March 7, 2024 and April 18, 2024. "Intuit" means Intuit Inc., its subsidiaries, employees, agents and counsel, including any address at intuit.com. "The Department" means the Department of Attorney General, including the Consumer Protection Team and any other division or bureau. "Communications" includes email with attachments, letters, meeting notes, memoranda, and entries in any complaint or case management system. Unless an item states otherwise, the period is January 1, 2022 through the date of your search.

Not requested: the text of complaints or attachments submitted by consumers. This request is for the Department's own records of what it did.

Records requested, in order of priority:

1. Count and log. An existing count, log extract, or list of complaint numbers, receipt dates and dispositions for consumer complaints received by the Department from January 1, 2020 through the date of your search that concern Intuit's TurboTax or ProSeries software and the Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit, with complainants' personal identifying information redacted.

2. What the Department told consumers. The Department's outgoing acknowledgments, responses, closing letters and referral letters on those complaints, and any template or form response used for them, with complainants' personal identifying information redacted.

3. What the Department asked Intuit, and what Intuit said. All communications between the Department and Intuit concerning the Issue, including any inquiry the Department sent, any response, and any information Intuit supplied about the number of affected Michigan customers, notification of customers, refunds or amended returns, with complainants' names and contact details redacted.

4. Referrals to Treasury. All records of the referral of any complaint or inquiry concerning the Issue to the Department of Treasury, including the referral to Treasury's Bureau of Tax Policy on or about May 7, 2026, any response received from Treasury, and any further action taken or decided, excluding the complainant's own submission and attachments and with the complainant's name and contact details redacted.

5. Whether an inquiry was opened. Records reflecting whether the Department opened, declined to open, or closed any inquiry or investigation under the Michigan Consumer Protection Act, MCL 445.901 et seq., or otherwise, concerning the Issue, including intake or evaluation memoranda, closing memoranda, and any notice to Intuit. If the Department withholds investigating records, please release the nonexempt portions under MCL 15.244 and describe what is withheld, including the dates on which any inquiry was opened and closed.

6. Press, legislative and public inquiries. Records of inquiries to the Department from the press, from members of the Legislature, or from the public concerning the Issue, and the Department's responses, including any public statement the Department prepared or issued.

Format. Under MCL 15.234(1)(c), please provide the records electronically, as native email files (.eml or .msg) with attachments where they exist, otherwise as searchable PDF.

Fees. I ask that the Department waive or reduce fees under MCL 15.234(2).
